newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares firm 0.93 pct on new govt prospect.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares firm 0.93 pct on new govt prospect.

text.p: Istanbul shares ended higher on Tuesday as prices recovered from day's lows on the prospect of a new secularist government alliance to replace the ruling Islamist-led coalition, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 closed 13 points, or 0.93 percent higher at 1,408 on dissident government MP Yalim Erez's remarks that his planned alternative coalition excluding the Islamists would aim to rule rather than hold early elections. It earlier dived 2.3 percent to a low of 1,363.
Brokers said Erez's and other opposition leaders' comments on forming a secularist pact reduced uncertainty to some extent and prompted buying in the afternoon.
Trade volume rose to 10.92 trillion lira ($79.7 million) from Monday's 7.11 trillion ($52.1 million).

"Today's rise was not a healthy one because the index may still ease to 1,300-1,350 range unless there is a concrete development in the political arena," said Mustafa Arar, general manager of Ari securities.
"The existing coalition either stays strong without a problem or a solid alternative comes up," he said.
Arar added that trade remained dominated by punters due to the continuing liquidity shortage in the market.

Erez said after meeting two opposition leaders that he planned to discuss his coalition proposal as soon as possible with Tansu Ciller, deputy prime minister and leader of the conservative True Path Party (DYP).
It was not clear how many DYP deputies would support Erez's plan, but Yilmaz said there was support within the DYP.
Erez and another DYP minister had resigned in late April in protest at the Islamists' failure to back an army-inspired crackdown on religious activism.
The index had dived 3.33 percent on Monday as worries over the future of the ruling coalition mounted, bringing losses to 8.9 percent since April 24 when the market opened after a 6-1/2 day holiday.
